findings.effect: Android's default is null (CarrierConfigManager.java:2827,12152), and Google's default entry sets this key, so the key is never unset on a served bundle. The one reader is ImsPhoneCallTracker (:2022-2061, :3243-3291). It matches code and lower-cased message by prefix, and an empty message matches every message for that code. The mapped code reaches only the disconnect cause, the precise cause and metrics; every redial reads the raw code (:3625-3640, :3795-3824). ImsStack never reads the key. Read, not tested, with the tracker's lines as on the phone's code from 2026-11-01.
findings.risk: No harm was found. From holding, these SIMs follow Google's own entry both ways, and a value that changes little still stops beating what Google later writes. Nothing here says what the network does.
